title: GPE: Global Position Embedding for Trajectory Similarity Computation

problem.claim: Trajectory similarity computation is a fundamental functionality in trajectory data mining, and position embedding is critical to learning-based trajectory similarity models.

gap.claim: Existing position-embedding methods do not simultaneously satisfy global, continuous, unique, and dynamic properties, limiting trajectory similarity computation in local and global scenarios.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes the lambda-base circular system to embed positions on a circle.
The paper introduces GPE, a multi-base global embedding method for encoding global positions into vectors.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on five real-world datasets with nine baseline methods report state-of-the-art performance for GPE across four key downstream-task evaluations.

narrative_sequence.summary: Trajectory similarity computation is important in trajectory data mining and location-based services.
Position embedding affects the performance of learning-based trajectory similarity models.
Existing methods lack the full set of global, continuous, unique, and dynamic properties.
The authors propose a circular position-embedding system and the GPE global embedding method.
Experiments across five datasets, nine baselines, and four evaluations report state-of-the-art performance.

source_observation.claim: The abstract reports that embedding quality significantly affects downstream model performance.

interpretation.claim: Representation design can be a central lever for improving trajectory-similarity systems.

application.claim: When developing trajectory-similarity models, evaluate and improve the position-embedding component rather than focusing only on the downstream model.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the reported embedding properties are sufficient for all datasets or applications.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the four key evaluations.
The abstract does not provide quantitative results, dataset names, baseline names, or experimental conditions.
The abstract does not describe the lambda-base system or GPE algorithm in implementation detail.
